title: LatentProtocol
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 methods between the Latent engine and its UI. Each method has <Method>Params and <Method>Result. Phase 0 surface only.

NotificationName.description: Engine → UI messages without an id. Calling one as a method is a -32601 error.

PhotoId.description: Stable catalog id (SQLite rowid), so an i64. LTHM binary frames carry it in a u32 slot (protocol/frames.md), which caps thumbnails at 4294967295: catalog.thumbnail and catalog.thumbnails answer -32602 for a larger id instead of sending a frame with a truncated target. Every other method takes the full range.

Op.description: One entry of the op-stack. `op` names a definition from ops.describe; `params` validates against that definition's schema. The reserved name `"group"` is the exception: it has no definition and no params, and is a layer — one mask, one opacity, and the adjustments under them in `ops` (PROMPT.md 3.7).

ops.description: Groups only, and always present on one (empty included): the adjustments that share this layer's mask, in the user's order. They render as one branch off the group's input and are blended back through the mask once, so a feathered edge is crossed once however many adjustments the layer holds. A child is a develop op — no geometry, no generative op, no nested group — and carries only `enabled`: `mask` and `opacity` belong to the group.

opacity.description: Layer opacity 0–100; absent means 100. The op's output is mixed into its input by opacity × mask; on a group it scales the whole layer.

result.description: Generative ops only (PROMPT.md 3.5): the cached raster this op produced, as a PNG path relative to the photo's raster dir ($XDG_DATA_HOME/latent/rasters/<sha256>/, keyed by the file's hash) — `generative/<opId>.png`. Absent until a generative.run has landed; the op renders as if it were not there until then. A client round-trips it untouched.

inputHash.description: Generative ops only: sha256 over the ops that produced `result`'s input, the op's mask and its params. Engine-owned; a client round-trips it untouched.

resultRect.description: Generative ops only: `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` of `result` inside the content rect, normalised 0..1 — where the crop was cut from and where the composite puts it back. Engine-owned.

ops.description: Groups only (`op` is `group`): the adjustments under this group's mask, in the user's order. They render as one branch off the group's input and are blended back through the mask once. A child carries `enabled` and its params; `mask` and `opacity` belong to the group, and a group is never a child of a group.

stale.description: Engine-derived, never stored: `inputHash` no longer matches the stack, so `result` was made from other pixels. A stale op still renders its last result — re-running is always explicit (generative.run).

Mask.description: A per-op mask: components combined top-down with add / subtract / intersect (PROMPT.md §3.7). Rasters live in the engine; the UI only ever sees them as LMSK frames from mask.preview. An op with a mask renders as mix(in, op(in), mask × opacity).

space.description: Which space every component's coordinates are normalised over. `image` is 0..1 across the uncropped, unrotated, untransformed photo — the size photo.open reports, camera orientation already applied — and is what the engine writes and renders: a mask painted on the subject stays on it when crop, straighten, rotate, flip or the Transform sliders move afterwards. `content` is the pre-2026-09-16 convention, 0..1 over the content rect of whatever view drew it; only a sidecar written before this change holds one, and the engine converts it through the stack's own geometry the first time it opens the photo and writes `image` back. Absent means `image`: a client that does not send the field is a client that never applied geometry either. The two spaces coincide for an uncropped photo.

MaskComponentKind.description: Mirrors Lightroom's Masking panel, plus the two kinds Lightroom has no answer for. Detected kinds (subject, sky, background, objects, people, text, depth, trails) rasterise through mask.detect as a job; the rest rasterise inline from their params. `depth` is the odd one: its raster is the scene's depth map rather than a selection, and `params.range` bands it in the shader, so moving the range is a slider and not another model run. `trails` is the other: it runs a line detector rather than a model, so it needs nothing from the model store, and because its raster is derived from the frame and its seed stroke alone, the same component detects the aircraft trails in every photo it is copied to.

MaskComponent.description: The engine always emits `id` and `mode`. It tolerates a write without them (generates an id, defaults mode to `add`) as leniency for scripts, not as contract: a UI sends both.

feather.description: Edge softness 0–100; absent = 0 for AI/luminance/color, the tool's own default for brush/linear/radial.

params.description: Kind-specific, all coordinates normalised 0..1 over the image (Mask.space), never over the cropped view: use ViewRenderResult.imageTransform to put one on a canvas. A brush's `size` is a diameter as a fraction of the image's long edge, in the same space. linear: {start:[x,y], end:[x,y]}. radial: {center:[x,y], radius:[rx,ry], angle}. luminance: {range:[lo,hi], smoothness}. color: {samples:[[r,g,b]], range, smoothness}. brush: {size, flow} plus engine-owned `strokeData` (the stroke list — it lives in the op so one undo drops one stroke) and `strokes` (the path it is mirrored to); strokes are appended with mask.stroke, never sent whole. objects: {box:[x0,y0,x1,y1]} or {points:[[x,y]]}. people: {person, parts?}. text: {prompt}. trails: {seed:[[x,y]] — the stroke drawn along one aircraft trail, which is what the detector measures every other streak against; a path and not a box, because a trail is a line and a box around a diagonal one is mostly sky. At most 256 points, thinned by the client — plus sensitivity 0–100 (how much dimmer than the seed a streak may be), minLength 1–100 (shortest streak kept, as a percentage of the long edge) and grow 0–100 (margin drawn around each streak, as a percentage of a two-hundredth of the long edge — a trail is two or three pixels wide and the mask is meant to hug it). AI kinds carry {model, sourceHash, raster: <cached PNG path relative to the photo's raster dir>} once rasterised and `error` after a failed detect. A client round-trips strokeData, strokes, raster and error untouched.

state.description: Engine-owned. ready = raster cached for these params; pending = mask.detect job running; stale = params or source changed since the raster (not auto re-run); failed = last job failed.

componentId.description: One component's raster instead of the combined mask.

viewId.description: Size the raster like this view's proxy so the overlay maps 1:1 onto the frame. Absent = the photo's proxy size.

contentRect.description: [x, y, width, height] of the image inside the proxy, in proxy pixels. Where the raster's photo pixels are; zoomed in it runs outside the frame, so x and y can be negative and the rect can be wider than the frame.

imageTransform.description: Same matrix as ViewRenderResult.imageTransform, for the raster's own pixel grid: image-normalised → raster pixel.

coverage.description: Fraction 0..1 of pixels above 50 %, so a client can tell an empty mask from a failed one.

MaskPreviewResult.description: Sent after exactly one LMSK frame on the calling socket (protocol/frames.md). `width`/`height` are the view's full proxy size, letterbox included; `coverage` is measured over the image rect inside it. A component in `pending` or `failed` state contributes nothing to the combined raster; asking for its own raster is a -32602 error.

hint.description: Overrides the component's params for this run: {box}, {points}, {prompt}. Stored back into the component on success.

MaskDetectParams.description: Starts (or re-runs) the AI rasterisation of one component. The component goes `pending` immediately (stack.changed), the job ticks job.progress with kind "mask", and on completion the component is `ready` or `failed` (stack.changed again). Non-AI kinds are a -32602 error.

DepthEstimateParams.description: Runs monocular depth estimation over the photo (PROMPT.md 3.8) and caches the map as `depth.png` in the photo's raster dir ($XDG_DATA_HOME/latent/rasters/<sha256>/, keyed by the file's hash). Ticks job.progress with kind "depth" and publishes depth.changed when it lands. The map belongs to the photo rather than to the stack — it is not edit state, it costs no undo step, and no slider can make it stale — so re-running it is always an explicit ask. A `relight` op renders nothing until one exists, and a `depth` mask component contributes nothing.

DepthStatusParams.description: Whether the photo has a depth map right now. A UI asks this when it opens a photo; after that depth.changed says when one lands.

model.description: What produced the map. Absent when there is none.

DepthPreviewParams.description: Sends the photo's depth map as one LDPT binary frame on the calling socket (protocol/frames.md), then answers with its size. A photo with no map is a -32602 error.

model.description: What produced the map — the model's store name, or the stub.

DepthPreviewResult.description: The LDPT frame's own size. Unlike a mask preview this is image space and has no letterbox: 0..1 over the uncropped photo, so a client draws it through `imageTransform` like any other mask coordinate.

DepthChangedParams.description: Broadcast when a depth.estimate job lands. Not a stack change — nothing in the op-stack moved — but every relight op on the photo starts rendering, so a client re-renders its view.

GenerativeRunParams.description: Runs one generative op (PROMPT.md 3.5). The engine renders the ops below it, crops the op's mask bounding box plus padding to at most 1536 px on the long edge, hands the crop and the mask to the backend, and stores the result as `Op.result`. Ticks job.progress with kind "generative" and publishes stack.changed when it lands. Nothing else ever starts a run: an op whose `stale` is true keeps rendering its last result until this is called again. An op that is not generative is a -32602 error, and so is a masked generative op with no mask. `denoise` and `upscale` are the whole-frame ops (issues #51, #52): they take no mask, the whole frame goes to the backend, and `upscale`'s raster comes back larger than the photo — every coordinate on the wire stays normalised over the uncropped photo regardless.

GenerativeStatusResult.description: Whether a generative run can succeed right now, and why not. A UI shows `message`/`hint` instead of letting a run fail silently.

backend.description: What the ops' `backend: "auto"` resolves to on this daemon.

stub.description: LATENT_GENERATIVE_STUB=1: runs answer with a blurred stand-in and never touch ComfyUI.

models.description: Weight files under the ComfyUI workspace's models/{checkpoints,unet,diffusion_models}. What an op's `model` param may name.

ready.description: Every weight file the graph loads is installed.

items.description: [x, y] normalised 0..1, optional pressure 0..1 as third element.

size.description: Brush diameter as a fraction of the image's long edge; absent = the component's params.size.

transient.description: True for every segment of one pointer-down; the first non-transient call (pointer-up) snapshots, so a stroke undoes as one step.

MaskStrokeParams.description: Appends a stroke segment to a brush component. The engine owns the stroke list and its raster; the UI never uploads pixels. Only brush components accept strokes (-32602 otherwise).

ExportFormat.description: jpeg is 8-bit with the ICC in APP2; tiff16 and png are 16 bits per channel; avif is 10-bit AV1. The UI builds its format menu from this enum.

ExportColorSpace.description: The output profile. The engine converts from its linear working space in the last GPU pass and embeds the matching ICC, generated by lcms2 from the same primaries and curve.

longEdge.description: Fit the long side to this many pixels. Wins over width/height.

dpi.description: Metadata only — JFIF density, PNG pHYs, TIFF resolution. It never changes the pixel count.

ExportResize.description: Absent or empty means native resolution: the crop rect at sensor pixels. width and height together are a box the image is fitted inside, aspect kept. Resampling happens on the GPU in linear light, before the output curve.

ExportSharpen.description: Output sharpening, Lightroom's three targets. It is the last pass before the colour transform and is not part of the develop; absent means none.

photoIds.description: Catalog rows. A photo that is not open is decoded for the export and dropped again; an open one keeps its texture.

quality.description: JPEG and AVIF only; ignored by the lossless formats. Default 90.

outputDir.description: Created if it does not exist.

fileNameTemplate.description: `{name}` is the source file's stem, `{index}` its 1-based position in this run, `{ext}` the format's extension. Default `{name}`. Path separators are stripped — a template names a file, never a path — and the extension is forced.

ExportRunParams.description: Starts a batch export and returns immediately. Progress arrives as job.progress kind `export`, whose `message` is the file currently being written; job.cancel stops it between photos.

total.description: How many files the job will write — photoIds.length, so a bar can size itself before the first progress arrives.

OpParamSpec.description: One slider/control of an op, in Lightroom terms.

OpParamDisplay.description: How a generated panel should draw this param. Advisory: a UI that ignores it still renders a correct control from `type`, `min`, `max` and `step`.

kind.description: `slider` is the default control. `kelvin` is a white-balance temperature slider, `curve` a tone-curve editor, `hsl` an eight-band colour mixer, `toggle` a checkbox, `text` a free-text field — a generative prompt or a model name, drawn by a hand-built panel.

tint.description: Gradient to paint under the track, the way Lightroom tints Temp blue→yellow and Tint green→magenta.

section.description: Lightroom's Edit-panel section this op is drawn in. The display name of `panel`, and the heading a generated panel groups under.

order.description: Position inside `section`, ascending, following Lightroom's slider order. Ops without one sort last, then by name.

maskable.description: The op accepts `mask` and `opacity` (every develop op). Geometry ops, generative ops that own their region, and the whole-frame `denoise`/`upscale` are not maskable; absent = false.

Histogram.description: 256 bins per channel over the 8-bit display pixels, plus the share of pixels at either end. On ViewRenderResult it is counted over the image rect of the frame that was just sent, letterbox excluded, so it belongs to those pixels; on StackGetResult it comes from whatever frame the view last drew, which is one render behind the edit that is being answered.

catalogPath.description: Absolute path of the SQLite catalog this daemon opened. A UI shows which catalog it is on; a test asserts it is the throwaway one and not ~/.local/share/latent/catalog.db.

mcpUrl.description: Streamable-HTTP endpoint of the engine's MCP server, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7801/mcp. Absent when the daemon was started with --no-mcp or the SDK failed to load.

PhotoOpenResult.description: Opening a file catalogs it, so `catalog` carries the row and a client never has to follow photo.open with catalog.get. It is absent only when the engine opened a file it did not catalog.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the raw file, as stored in the sidecar.

sidecarLoaded.description: True when an existing .latent sidecar was read and its stack restored.

depthReady.description: True when `depth.png` in the photo's raster dir ($XDG_DATA_HOME/latent/rasters/<sha256>/, keyed by the file's hash) was there and is loaded. False means a relight op would render nothing until depth.estimate is called.

historyIndex.description: Which snapshot of the undo stack this is, counting the photo's opening state as 0. `revision` is a change counter that advances on every write, transient drag ticks included; this counts undo steps, so a slider drag moves it by one however many frames it took.

historyDepth.description: How many snapshots the undo stack holds, the opening state included, so `historyIndex + 1 == historyDepth` means nothing is left to redo.

label.description: What to call this step in the history list, when the caller knows something the diff cannot see: `Golden hour applied`, `Settings pasted`. Absent means the step is named after what it changed.

params.description: Omitted keys take the registry defaults; omitted entirely adds the op at defaults.

index.description: Insert position; end of stack — or of the group named by `parentId` — when omitted.

parentId.description: Add the op inside this group instead of at the top level, so it shares that layer's mask (PROMPT.md 3.7). The group's own `mask` and `opacity` win: both are ignored on the child. -32602 when the id is not a group, or when the op cannot sit in one.

transient.description: True when the add is the first tick of a slider drag: no history snapshot, no sidecar write, so the whole drag undoes as one step. The first non-transient update after it snapshots.

OpAddResult.description: The stack after the add, and the id the engine gave the new op — a caller that added into a group cannot find it by position.

params.description: Partial; merged into the op's params.

transient.description: True while a slider is being dragged: no history snapshot, no sidecar write. The first non-transient update after a drag snapshots.

mask.description: Full replacement, never a merge: a mask is an ordered list and merging two by index is not something a caller can reason about. `null` clears it.

opacity.description: Layer opacity 0–100; absent leaves it unchanged.

HistoryChange.description: One parameter this step moved. `from` and `to` are the parameter's own values, so the UI formats them with the spec ops.describe gave the control. A value that is not a scalar - a curve's point list - is reported as a change with neither, since a list of points is nothing a history row can show.

HistoryEntry.description: One op inside a `batch` step, described exactly as a step of its own would be. `opId` is what history.revertOp takes to put this one op back to what it was before the step, leaving the rest of the batch where it is.

HistoryStep.description: One snapshot of the undo stack, described by what it changed from the snapshot before it. Index 0 is the state the photo opened in, so its kind is `initial` and it has no changes. A drag is one step: the engine replaces the snapshot in place while it runs (StackGetResult.historyIndex).

op.description: The op this step is about, by name: `exposure`, `group`. Absent on `initial`, `reorder` and `batch`, which are about the stack rather than one entry.

label.description: What the caller called this step (StackSetParams.label) - `Golden hour applied`. A UI shows it instead of the name it would otherwise derive, because the caller knew something the diff cannot see.

entries.description: `batch` only: the ops this step touched, one each. A preset moves a dozen at once and naming the step after any one of them would be a lie, so they are listed - which is also what lets a UI unfold the row and revert one of them on its own (history.revertOp).

HistoryListResult.description: The whole undo stack of one photo, described. One entry per snapshot, oldest first; `index` is where the cursor sits, the same number StackGetResult.historyIndex carries.

HistoryJumpParams.description: Moves the undo cursor straight to one snapshot - clicking a row of the history list. Out of range is -32602; the step that is already current is accepted and changes nothing.

HistoryRevertOpParams.description: Puts one op back to what it was before step `index`, and leaves everything else where it is - unfolding a preset's row and taking back the one adjustment that did not suit the photo. It is an edit, not a cursor move: a new step is committed on top, so the revert itself undoes. -32602 when the step or the op is not there, or when `index` is 0, which has no state before it.

ViewOpenParams.description: A view is one canvas showing one photo at one proxy size. Frames for it arrive as LFRM binary frames tagged with viewId.

ViewRenderParams.description: Ask for a frame of the view's current state. Resizing happens here too.

geometry.description: How much of the geometry stage this frame applies. `stack` is the whole stack, the default. `full` renders the uncropped image: the crop op's rect and its straighten angle are bypassed so the crop tool can show what is being cropped away, while rotate, flip and Transform still apply because they move the whole image.

viewport.description: Zoom and pan. Sticky per view: send it when it changes, leave it out otherwise and the view stays where it was. It is not edit state — nothing about it reaches the stack or the sidecar.

scale.description: 1 is fit-to-view, the behaviour of every render before this field existed; 2 is twice that. A client computes 1:1 as imageWidth / (contentRect width at scale 1).

centerX.description: The image-normalised point the view is centred on. Sending neither centre, or a scale of 1, means fit: the image is centred the way it always was. The engine clamps the pan so a zoomed view never shows a bar it could fill with photo, and echoes what it used in the result.

insets.description: What the client floats over the frame — its panels — in frame pixels. A fitted photo is fitted into the view minus these and centred in what is left, so no panel covers it; a zoomed one still fills the whole frame and runs on behind them. Sticky per view like `viewport`, and not edit state. Absent or all-zero is the old behaviour: fit the whole view.

revision.description: Stack revision the frame was rendered from — the same counter as StackGetResult.revision. A client that coalesced slider drags compares it with the revision of the last stack.changed it saw to know whether the frame it is holding is the newest state or one render behind.

width.description: Size of the frame that was sent, so a client that dropped it still knows the view size.

contentRect.description: [x, y, width, height] of the image inside the proxy, in proxy pixels. Zoomed in it is larger than the frame and x/y go negative, so read it as signed numbers and not as a letterbox.

imageTransform.description: image-normalised → view pixel: a row-major 3×3 applied to (x, y, 1) with a homogeneous divide, so [m0 m1 m2 m3 m4 m5 m6 m7 m8] means px = (m0·x + m1·y + m2)/w, py = (m3·x + m4·y + m5)/w, w = m6·x + m7·y + m8. Projective and not affine, because the Transform sliders' keystone is. It carries crop, straighten, rotate, flip, Transform and the viewport's zoom and pan, so it converts a pointer to a mask coordinate (through its inverse) and a mask coordinate to a canvas pixel. Lens distortion is deliberately not in it: the radial term has no closed-form inverse, so the matrix is exact wherever lens_correction.distortion is 0, which is its default, and off by that term otherwise. Optional and additive: a client without it falls back to contentRect, which is the same thing whenever nothing is cropped.

viewport.description: The viewport this frame was rendered with, after clamping. Echoed so a client that asked for an out-of-range zoom or a pan past the edge shows what it got rather than what it wanted.

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock budget for the script. On expiry the engine interrupts it with KeyboardInterrupt and answers with an error result (`ok: false`, the traceback in `stderr`), never by dropping the call. Default 30000.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time the script took, measured around the interpreter call. The same number the run's python.finished carries. Optional only so a client written against an older engine still typechecks; latentd and the mock always send it.

value.description: repr() of the script's last expression, if any.

runId.description: Set when the engine streamed the run's output as python.output notifications. `stdout`/`stderr` still carry the complete streams, so a client that showed the live output replaces it with these when the call returns.

PythonOutputParams.description: Notification: output a still-running script has produced. Sent to the socket that issued python.run, before that call's result. Long scripts stream; a short one may answer with the result alone.

text.description: The chunk as written, newlines included. Never re-sent, never trimmed.

PythonFinishedParams.description: Notification: a run ended. Sent to the socket that issued python.run, after that run's last python.output and before the RPC result, so a console can close the output stream without waiting for the result to arrive.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time the script took. Matches the run's PythonRunResult.durationMs.

ok.description: False when the script raised or ran out of its timeoutMs budget; the traceback is in the result's stderr, not here.

StackChangedParams.description: Notification: the stack of a photo changed by any writer (UI, script, MCP). Carries the new state so the UI never re-fetches.

source.description: `ui` = the receiving client made this change itself; `external` = another socket did; `python`/`mcp` = a script or agent; `history` = undo/redo; `load` = sidecar restore on open.

client.description: Who caused the change, one step more specific than `source` and free-form so it can name a tool: `ui`, `external`, `python`, `mcp:<tool>` (e.g. `mcp:run_python`), `history`, `load`. Per socket like `source` is — the writer sees `ui`, the others `external`. A console prints it; nothing branches on it.

photoId.description: Set when the message concerns one photo (e.g. a clamped op param).

CatalogPhoto.description: One catalog row. `photoId` is the stable id used everywhere else.

capturedAt.description: ISO 8601 from EXIF; absent when unknown.

editedAt.description: ISO 8601 of the last non-transient stack change; absent when never edited.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the raw file, the same value photo.open returns. Present once the engine has hashed the file — an import registers a row before hashing it, so a freshly imported row can lack it until it is opened.

RunId.description: One python.run execution. Unique per engine process, so a client can tell its own run's output from another socket's.

CatalogImportParams.description: Registers files (or every photo in the given directories) in the catalog, then queues thumbnails and previews. Returns immediately; progress arrives as job.progress notifications. Idempotent per path — a row that already exists has its metadata refreshed and keeps its rating, flag and importedAt — so calling this again over a folder is how a rescan is spelled. Every directory in `paths` also becomes a watched root: photos that land in it later are catalogued without being asked for, and the watch is remembered across restarts. Single files never start a watch.

recursive.description: Descend into subdirectories. Default true; only directories in `paths` are affected.

thumbnailJobId.description: The thumbnail job the import queues behind itself, reserved up front so a client can follow both from the one result. Its job.progress carries parentJobId = jobId. It always reports, even when the import found nothing or was cancelled — then with total 0. Absent from an engine that does not queue thumbnails.

previewJobId.description: The preview job: one full decode per imported photo, scaled into the engine's preview cache so opening any of them later costs a file read instead of a second of LibRaw. Runs on a thread of its own — the app stays usable — and reports job.progress of kind `previews` with parentJobId = jobId. Cancellable like any other job. Absent from an engine that does not prewarm.

PreviewPrioritizeParams.description: Photos to decode first. A running preview job takes these out of its queue before anything else, so the photo being looked at is ready ahead of the rest of the import. Naming a photo that is not queued, or that already has a preview, is not an error — the list is a hint. Each call replaces the previous one.

prioritized.description: How many ids the engine recorded. The hint is kept whether or not a preview job is running.

PhotoResolutionParams.description: A photo the engine opened from its cached preview now has the full-resolution decode behind it. The frame the client holds came off the proxy, so the views of this photo need re-rendering to show the sharp one. Sent only for a photo that was opened from a preview, and only once.

CatalogListParams.description: Catalog rows, filtered and sorted. Every property narrows the result; combining them is an AND. Rows with equal sort keys are ordered by filename ascending, then by photoId ascending, so paging is stable and the same list never reshuffles between calls.

folder.description: Exact folder match; omit for every photo.

photoIds.description: Exactly these rows, in the list's sort order. Ids that are not in the catalog are left out rather than erroring. Useful for refreshing a selection without re-listing a page.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match over filename and camera. Empty string matches everything.

watched.description: A watched root covers this folder, so photos that land in it are catalogued on their own. False means the folder is only as fresh as its last catalog.import over it, which is what a rescan is.

CatalogCollectionSetParams.description: Create (name without collectionId), rename (both), add/remove members, or delete a collection.

CatalogThumbnailParams.description: Sends an LTHM binary frame (JPEG, target = photoId) before the result. Cached on disk by the engine; generated from the embedded preview when the raw has one, else from a fast half-size decode. A photoId above 4294967295 does not fit the frame's u32 target and is refused with -32602.

CatalogThumbnailsParams.description: Batch form of catalog.thumbnail: one LTHM binary frame per photo that has one, all sent before the result. A filmstrip asks for the page it is about to draw in one call instead of one call per cell. An id above 4294967295 does not fit the frame's u32 target: the whole call is refused with -32602 rather than listed in `missing`, because it is a malformed request and not a photo that failed to render.

size.description: Long edge in px, the same for every photo in the batch. Default 256.

CatalogThumbnailsResult.description: Sent after the frames. A photo that produced no thumbnail — unknown id, unreadable file, decode failure — is listed in `missing` and has no frame; the call itself does not fail.

CatalogRemoveParams.description: Removes catalog rows: the database entries, their thumbnails and their collection memberships. Files on disk and their .latent sidecars are never touched — re-importing the same path brings the photo back (with a new photoId). Ids that are not in the catalog are ignored.

JobCancelParams.description: Asks a running job to stop at its next safe point. Work already done stands: a cancelled import keeps the photos it registered.

cancelled.description: True when a running job was asked to stop; false when the job is unknown or already finished. The job's last job.progress then has `finished: true` and `state: "cancelled"`.

CatalogChangedParams.description: Notification: catalog rows changed. Clients re-list what they show.

JobProgressParams.description: Notification for long-running engine work (import, thumbnails, later export).

parentJobId.description: The job that queued this one — set on the thumbnail job an import spawns, absent on a job nobody spawned. A progress UI nests the child under its parent instead of showing two unrelated bars.

state.description: How the job stands. `running` while `finished` is false; one of the other three on the last notification. Absent means `running` until finished, then `done` — so a client written before this field keeps working.

JobResult.description: What the job produced, on its last job.progress only — absent while it runs, and absent from a job whose output is the catalog itself (import, thumbnails). Every field is optional: a merge answers `photoId` and `path`, a merge preview answers `previewUrl` and `previewPath` and no photoId.

photoId.description: The catalog row the job created — the merged image. Open it like any other photo.

previewUrl.description: http://127.0.0.1:/preview/.png — the engine serves the file it just wrote over its own listener, so a renderer can put it in an without a file:// read.

MergeDeghost.description: Lightroom's Deghost Amount. The reference is the middle exposure; a pixel whose radiance differs from it by more than the level's threshold (low 1.0 EV, medium 0.5 EV, high 0.25 EV) drops that frame's contribution.

MergeProjection.description: Lightroom's Layout projection. `perspective` composes on a flat canvas; `cylindrical` and `spherical` pre-warp each frame around the focal length read from EXIF before composing.

MergeTrailBlend.description: `lighten` takes the brightest frame per pixel, which is what draws the trails. `average` takes the mean: one long exposure with sqrt(N) less noise and no trails.

MergeTrailForeground.description: Where the still half of the picture comes from. `lighten` treats it like everything else, so it also collects every frame's hot pixels and any headlight that swept the ground. `firstFrame` keeps frame one there and lets a later frame in only where it is `foregroundThreshold` brighter.

MergeHdrParams.description: Merges 2..7 exposure-bracketed photos into one linear 16-bit TIFF, registers it in the catalog and answers its photoId on the job's last job.progress. Tone is the user's job: no auto settings are applied.

photoIds.description: 2 to 7 exposures of one scene, in any order. Fewer or more is a -32602.

outputPath.description: Absolute path of the TIFF to write. Default: `<first source without extension>-HDR.tif` next to the sources.

MergePanoramaParams.description: Stitches 2..12 overlapping photos into one linear 16-bit TIFF and registers it in the catalog.

photoIds.description: 2 to 12 overlapping frames, in shooting order. Fewer or more is a -32602; the cap is memory, not the algorithm.

boundaryWarp.description: Warps the mosaic toward the crop rectangle instead of throwing the edges away. 0 = no warp, 100 = the valid content is stretched to fill the rectangle.

MergeHdrPanoramaParams.description: Detects the bracket groups by their exposure pattern, merges each to HDR, then stitches the results. Every group must hold the same number of frames and the same EV offsets.

photoIds.description: Every frame of every bracket, in shooting order. 4 to 48; the groups are found from the exposure pattern, not from the order alone.

MergeStarTrailParams.description: Stacks 2..500 frames of one night sequence into one linear 16-bit TIFF and registers it in the catalog. The frames are folded in as they decode and dropped again, so the count is bounded by patience rather than by memory. No alignment and no deghosting: a star trail merge assumes a tripod, and registering the frames would straighten the trails.

photoIds.description: The sequence in shooting order. Order is what the comet decay and the gap fill read; a lighten stack alone does not care.

gapFill.description: Synthetic sub-frames between each pair, bridging the camera's write time so a trail is a line instead of a dotted one. Each is the later frame pulled back a fraction of the inter-frame shift, which is measured by correlating the two frames' high-passed luminance: a frame whose landscape outweighs its stars correlates at zero shift and the fill does nothing, and near the celestial pole the motion is a rotation that a shift only approximates.

foregroundThreshold.description: How far above frame one a pixel has to be before `foreground: "firstFrame"` lets it through, as a percentage of a tenth of the white level. Ignored by the other foreground rule and by `average`.

decay.description: Comet tails. 0 weights every frame the same; 100 fades the oldest frame 6 stops down, so each trail brightens toward where the star ended up.

outputPath.description: Absolute path of the TIFF to write. Default: `<first source without extension>-Trails.tif` next to the sources.

MergePreviewParams.description: The same merge at preview size, from the raws' embedded JPEGs instead of a full decode — seconds instead of minutes. Writes a PNG and names it in the job's last job.progress `result`; nothing is written to the catalog.

photoIds.description: The same ids the full merge would get.
